value.fallback: If Cast is not part of the escape sequence, equip The Swift Runner for movement value that does not depend on Cast timing.
value.limitation: The protection is short and depends on deliberate Cast timing.
value.reason: Brief invulnerability and movement speed make an action already used in combat safer.
value.recommendation: Equip The Messenger when Cast placement also serves as an escape or repositioning tool.

value.fallback: If maximum Life is already sufficient but repeated chip damage accumulates, equip The Wayward Son for room-to-room recovery.
value.limitation: It provides no scaling after the starting resources stop being the route constraint.
value.reason: Maximum Life and Magick help every weapon before the run offers any rewards.
value.recommendation: Equip Persistence in early progression and in any loadout that needs a larger starting buffer.

value.fallback: If no reachable Duo path is already present, use Excellence for broad rarity or The Champions to find a required Boon.
value.limitation: The card's activation condition and offer dependence make it useless to an unfinished core build.
value.reason: Additional Duo chance matters after both gods and prerequisite sets are represented.
value.recommendation: Activate The Queen when the planned build already contains reachable Duo prerequisites.

value.fallback: If the weakened starting board cannot reach the first Guardian reliably, equip the required combat cards directly.
value.limitation: The early route begins weaker and random cards may not support the selected aspect.
value.reason: Each guardian can add random inactive cards and raise the late-run ceiling.
value.recommendation: Activate Judgment for long routes when the starting board can survive until multiple guardians fall.

value.fallback: If targets will not remain inside Cast, spend the Grasp on a card that directly supports the aspect's primary move.
value.limitation: Mobile targets or a sequence that leaves Cast behind reduce its uptime.
value.reason: Its damage bonus rewards the same Cast placement used for control and Origination setup.
value.recommendation: Equip The Furies when the build keeps priority targets inside Cast.

value.fallback: If three Grasp does not fit or the longer slowdown is unnecessary, equip The Sorceress for a cheaper channel-speed bonus.
value.limitation: Its three-Grasp cost is hard to justify for quick taps or normal-move builds.
value.reason: The slowdown protects deliberate charging and aiming during active encounters.
value.recommendation: Equip Eternity when long Omega channels need a larger reaction window.

value.fallback: If fatal mistakes end the run, equip Death. If ordinary damage is the larger problem, equip Persistence.
value.limitation: Three Grasp adds no room-clear speed and the protected hits are limited.
value.reason: Its encounter shields prevent the first mistakes in each guardian fight.
value.recommendation: Equip The Lovers when guardian hits are the main reason otherwise stable runs fail.

value.fallback: If Sprint positioning causes more damage than Omega channels, equip The Swift Runner instead.
value.limitation: A build that rarely channels Omega moves gains little from the slot.
value.reason: Its one-Grasp charge-speed bonus shortens the exposed part of every Omega action.
value.recommendation: Equip The Sorceress while learning Omega moves or using an Omega-heavy aspect.

value.fallback: If the correct god already appears but the needed Boon does not, equip The Champions to reroll that god's choices.
value.limitation: It cannot reroll the choices inside an offered Boon and costs three Grasp.
value.reason: Location rerolls can replace an unwanted door before the next encounter is chosen.
value.recommendation: Equip The Enchantress when route rewards and permanent resources matter more than fishing for one Boon.

value.fallback: If Divinity's activation pattern breaks the combat core, use Excellence when five Grasp fits or keep the core unchanged.
value.limitation: The activation layout can cost more useful cards than the rarity increase returns.
value.reason: Epic Boon access improves ordinary offers without requiring a specific god pair.
value.recommendation: Activate Divinity when the board condition fits a completed combat loadout.

value.fallback: If burst damage ends the night before room healing can help, equip Persistence for a larger starting Life buffer.
value.limitation: It cannot prevent burst damage or restore enough Life during one guardian encounter.
value.reason: Room-to-room healing repairs repeated small mistakes for only one Grasp.
value.recommendation: Equip The Wayward Son when room damage is the main source of failed routes.

value.fallback: Only after intentionally removing every Death Defiance should Strength replace Death for its low-Life damage and defense.
value.limitation: Four Grasp is inefficient when the run already finishes without consuming the effect.
value.reason: A guaranteed extra recovery protects an otherwise successful progression attempt.
value.recommendation: Equip Death until routes and guardians clear without using its Death Defiance.

value.fallback: While learning routes or Fear conditions, equip Death instead so one fatal mistake does not end the night.
value.limitation: Removing Death Defiance makes mistakes harder to recover from and is poor beginner progression advice.
value.reason: Its damage reduction and damage bonus remain active together when the condition is intentionally met.
value.recommendation: Equip Strength only for a deliberate no-Death-Defiance loadout.

value.fallback: If the build reliably maintains two curses, equip Origination for damage that does not depend on staying low on Magick.
value.limitation: Fast Magick recovery or an Omega-only loop reduces its active time.
value.reason: It turns an expected low-Magick state into direct weapon damage.
value.recommendation: Equip The Huntress only when the normal Attack or Special remains useful at low Magick.

value.fallback: If the Death activation is unavailable but two curses stay active, equip Origination for predictable damage instead.
value.limitation: Its activation and random payoff make it less reliable than direct survival or resource cards.
value.reason: Critical chance can scale every eligible hit without reserving a core Boon slot.
value.recommendation: Activate Night when the loadout already creates the required Death effect and attacks often enough to use critical chance.

value.fallback: If five Grasp does not fit, use Persistence for a cheaper starting Magick buffer and secure regeneration from a Boon.
value.limitation: Five Grasp is expensive when the build spends little Magick or already has strong recovery.
value.reason: Passive regeneration keeps Omega and Hex actions available across long rooms and guardians.
value.recommendation: Equip The Unseen for aspects that repeatedly spend Magick and lack reliable recovery.

value.fallback: If the board cannot meet The Centaur's activation pattern, equip Persistence for immediate Life and Magick instead.
value.limitation: Late activation or short routes provide fewer growth intervals.
value.reason: Free maximum Life and Magick accumulate during the same rooms needed to finish a route.
value.recommendation: Activate The Centaur when the board can meet its condition without sacrificing the core loadout.

value.fallback: If permanent progression is still the priority, keep the resource reward or use The Enchantress to reroll its door before entering.
value.limitation: The result is random and spending the conversion sacrifices permanent progression value.
value.reason: Its conversions can rescue a route whose ordinary rewards do not support the current build.
value.recommendation: Equip The Artificer when permanent-resource doors are less valuable than immediate run power.

value.fallback: If a required functional Boon is still missing, equip The Champions instead of spending five Grasp on offer quality.
value.limitation: It improves offer quality rather than fixing missing core slots or survival.
value.reason: Higher rarity and Legendary access can raise the ceiling of every offered god package.
value.recommendation: Equip Excellence only after the board can afford five Grasp beyond the functional combat core.

value.fallback: If finding the correct reward door is harder than choosing within an offer, equip The Enchantress instead.
value.limitation: Four Grasp is excessive for builds that accept many gods and core-slot options.
value.reason: Choice rerolls directly improve the chance of completing the planned package after the correct reward appears.
value.recommendation: Equip The Champions when an aspect needs a particular core Boon or prerequisite.

value.fallback: If Magick runs out before the Hex can charge, equip The Unseen for regeneration instead.
value.limitation: The card needs its activation condition and adds little when the chosen Hex is not useful.
value.reason: Automatic Hex charge adds uses without forcing more Magick spending into the weapon sequence.
value.recommendation: Activate The Moon when Hex use is part of the planned combat loop.

value.fallback: If stationary Omega channels cause the damage taken, equip The Sorceress. If Cast is the main escape tool, equip The Messenger.
value.limitation: It does not protect a stationary channel or repair poor Sprint timing.
value.reason: One Grasp improves Sprint speed and lets Melinoe pass through most foes.
value.recommendation: Equip The Swift Runner for mobile aspects or routes where repositioning causes damage taken.

value.fallback: If no early shop purchase is planned, spend the five Grasp on a combat card that works in every room.
value.limitation: The value is lost when early shops or useful purchases do not appear.
value.reason: Starting Gold converts five Grasp into immediate shop flexibility.
value.recommendation: Equip The Boatman when the route has early shops worth funding.

value.fallback: If the Boon plan cannot keep two curses on the same target, spend the five Grasp on unconditional survival or Magick support.
value.limitation: Five Grasp produces no value until both curses remain active on the same target.
value.reason: The damage bonus rewards a repeatable two-curse package across weapon, Cast, Sprint, and support Boons.
value.recommendation: Equip Origination when the build can maintain curses from two Olympians on priority targets.

value.fallback: If only doors need rerolls, equip The Enchantress. If only Boon choices need rerolls, equip The Champions.
value.limitation: Its board activation condition competes with other zero-Grasp cards.
value.reason: General rerolls can repair either route rewards or an offered set of choices.
value.recommendation: Activate The Fates when flexible rerolls help both doors and choice screens.

cards.limitation: Its Grasp cost must fit alongside the other core cards before support cards are added.
cards.reason: The Furies adds damage to the Cast that already controls the aspect's target area.

cards.limitation: Its Grasp cost must fit alongside the other core cards before support cards are added.

cards.limitation: Its Grasp cost must fit alongside the other core cards before support cards are added.
cards.reason: The Unseen restores the Magick needed to repeat the aspect's Omega sequence.

cards.limitation: Its Grasp cost must fit alongside the other core cards before support cards are added.
cards.reason: Persistence adds a reliable Life buffer without changing the aspect's combat sequence.

cards.limitation: Its Grasp cost must fit alongside the other core cards before support cards are added.
cards.reason: Death protects route progress while the aspect's positioning and boss windows are still being learned.

value.constraint: If current Grasp cannot hold the full list, keep core cards first, then add Persistence and Death before other support cards.

rewardDecisionRules.reason: Surviving the route preserves all existing build value and progression rewards.

rewardDecisionRules.reason: The permanent resource advances the A-to-Z route without sacrificing a required combat fix.

rewardDecisionRules.condition: The core Boon exists, the build survives, and no top Hammer or missing resource loop is offered.
rewardDecisionRules.reason: A level on the repeatedly used core effect is more reliable than filling an unused move slot.

rewardDecisionRules.condition: Every prerequisite set is satisfied and the offered Duo or Legendary directly supports the completed package.
rewardDecisionRules.reason: The rare target is worth taking only after the build already functions without it.

rewardDecisionRules.condition: The aspect's primary Attack, Special, Cast, Sprint, or Omega slot is still empty.
rewardDecisionRules.reason: A functional core move adds reliable damage now and unlocks later scaling choices.

rewardDecisionRules.condition: The combat sequence spends Magick repeatedly and no recovery source sustains one full room.
rewardDecisionRules.reason: The build stops working when Magick runs out, so recovery comes before optional damage.

rewardDecisionRules.condition: The core Boon is secured and one of the three recommended compatible Hammers is offered.
rewardDecisionRules.reason: A top Hammer changes the weapon itself and is harder to replace than another non-core Boon or one level.

rewardDecisionRules.condition: Current Life or Death Defiance cannot reliably cover the next guardian.
rewardDecisionRules.reason: Surviving the route preserves all existing build value and progression rewards.

rewardDecisionRules.condition: A named permanent unlock is the current progression target and the build already clears ordinary rooms safely.
rewardDecisionRules.reason: The permanent resource advances the A-to-Z route without sacrificing a required combat fix.

rewardDecisionRules.condition: The core Boon exists, the build survives, and no top Hammer or missing resource loop is offered.
rewardDecisionRules.reason: A level on the repeatedly used core effect is more reliable than filling an unused move slot.

rewardDecisionRules.condition: Every prerequisite set is satisfied and the offered Duo or Legendary directly supports the completed package.
rewardDecisionRules.reason: The rare target is worth taking only after the build already functions without it.

rewardPriorities.reason: Fill the aspect's special damage slot before spending rewards on optional scaling.

fallback.limitation: Another attack boon would replace this choice rather than stack with it.
fallback.reason: Flutter Strike is the stronger low-investment, full-string fallback. At Common level 1, its 80% adds 164 to the 205-damage string, four more than eight Wave Strike splashes, and it remains ahead through level 3 against one nearby target. Wave Strike overtakes at level 4, on cancelled strings, and whenever splashes hit extra foes. Backstab and Hammer damage modifiers are additive, so they raise the direct result without changing this comparison.

preferred.limitation: Another attack boon would replace this choice rather than stack with it.
preferred.reason: Wave Strike is the strongest upgraded Attack plan for the Blades' eight-hit normal string: 20 + 20 + five times 15 + 90 = 205 raw damage. At Common level 1, eight 20-damage splashes add 160, narrowly below Flutter Strike's 164. At level 4, eight 35-damage splashes add 280, above Flutter Strike's 266.5. It also wins on the 15- and 20-damage opening hits and can damage grouped foes. Prioritize Poms on it. This comparison assumes each unique hit clears the 0.033-second cooldown and its splash lands.

fallback.limitation: Another attack boon would replace this choice rather than stack with it.
fallback.reason: Flutter Strike is the stronger low-investment, full-string fallback. At Common level 1, its 80% adds 164 to the 205-damage string, four more than eight Wave Strike splashes, and it remains ahead through level 3 against one nearby target. Wave Strike overtakes at level 4, on cancelled strings, and whenever splashes hit extra foes. Backstab and Hammer damage modifiers are additive, so they raise the direct result without changing this comparison.

preferred.limitation: Another attack boon would replace this choice rather than stack with it.
preferred.reason: Wave Strike is the strongest upgraded Attack plan for the Blades' eight-hit normal string: 20 + 20 + five times 15 + 90 = 205 raw damage. At Common level 1, eight 20-damage splashes add 160, narrowly below Flutter Strike's 164. At level 4, eight 35-damage splashes add 280, above Flutter Strike's 266.5. It also wins on the 15- and 20-damage opening hits and can damage grouped foes. Prioritize Poms on it. This comparison assumes each unique hit clears the 0.033-second cooldown and its splash lands.

boonRankings.reason: Wave Strike is the strongest upgraded Attack plan for the Blades' eight-hit normal string: 20 + 20 + five times 15 + 90 = 205 raw damage. At Common level 1, eight 20-damage splashes add 160, narrowly below Flutter Strike's 164. At level 4, eight 35-damage splashes add 280, above Flutter Strike's 266.5. It also wins on the 15- and 20-damage opening hits and can damage grouped foes. Prioritize Poms on it. This comparison assumes each unique hit clears the 0.033-second cooldown and its splash lands.

boonRankings.reason: Flutter Strike is the stronger low-investment, full-string fallback. Wave Strike overtakes at level 4, on cancelled strings, and whenever splashes hit extra foes. Backstab and Hammer damage modifiers are additive, so they raise the direct result without changing this comparison.

rewardDecisionRules.condition: The aspect's primary Attack, Special, Cast, Sprint, or Omega slot is still empty.
rewardDecisionRules.reason: A functional core move adds reliable damage now and unlocks later scaling choices.

rewardDecisionRules.condition: The combat sequence spends Magick repeatedly and no recovery source sustains one full room.
rewardDecisionRules.reason: The build stops working when Magick runs out, so recovery comes before optional damage.

rewardDecisionRules.condition: The core Boon is secured and one of the three recommended compatible Hammers is offered.
rewardDecisionRules.reason: A top Hammer changes the weapon itself and is harder to replace than another non-core Boon or one level.

rewardDecisionRules.condition: Current Life or Death Defiance cannot reliably cover the next guardian.
rewardDecisionRules.reason: Surviving the route preserves all existing build value and progression rewards.

rewardDecisionRules.condition: A named permanent unlock is the current progression target and the build already clears ordinary rooms safely.
rewardDecisionRules.reason: The permanent resource advances the A-to-Z route without sacrificing a required combat fix.

rewardDecisionRules.condition: The core Boon exists, the build survives, and no top Hammer or missing resource loop is offered.
rewardDecisionRules.reason: A level on the repeatedly used core effect is more reliable than filling an unused move slot.

rewardDecisionRules.condition: Every prerequisite set is satisfied and the offered Duo or Legendary directly supports the completed package.
rewardDecisionRules.reason: The rare target is worth taking only after the build already functions without it.

rewardPriorities.reason: Fill the aspect's special damage slot before spending rewards on optional scaling.
Secure recovery before repeated Omega or Hex use makes the combat loop stall.
Take a compatible top-ranked Hammer after the first core Boon. No Hammer is required to make the build function.
Move maximum Life ahead of damage rewards when the current route cannot survive the next guardian reliably.
Use Poms after the core Boon exists so levels land on an effect the build repeatedly uses.
Pursue a Duo or Legendary only after the build already contains a valid choice from every prerequisite set.

strengths: Ranged homing volleys remain inside a rooting Cast

weaknesses: The volley loses value when a boss leaves Cast during the charge

rewardDecisionRules.condition: The aspect's primary Attack, Special, Cast, Sprint, or Omega slot is still empty.
rewardDecisionRules.reason: A functional core move adds reliable damage now and unlocks later scaling choices.

rewardDecisionRules.condition: The combat sequence spends Magick repeatedly and no recovery source sustains one full room.
rewardDecisionRules.reason: The build stops working when Magick runs out, so recovery comes before optional damage.

rewardDecisionRules.condition: The core Boon is secured and one of the three recommended compatible Hammers is offered.
rewardDecisionRules.reason: A top Hammer changes the weapon itself and is harder to replace than another non-core Boon or one level.

rewardDecisionRules.condition: Current Life or Death Defiance cannot reliably cover the next guardian.
rewardDecisionRules.reason: Surviving the route preserves all existing build value and progression rewards.

rewardDecisionRules.condition: A named permanent unlock is the current progression target and the build already clears ordinary rooms safely.
rewardDecisionRules.reason: The permanent resource advances the A-to-Z route without sacrificing a required combat fix.

rewardDecisionRules.condition: The core Boon exists, the build survives, and no top Hammer or missing resource loop is offered.
rewardDecisionRules.reason: A level on the repeatedly used core effect is more reliable than filling an unused move slot.

rewardDecisionRules.condition: Every prerequisite set is satisfied and the offered Duo or Legendary directly supports the completed package.
rewardDecisionRules.reason: The rare target is worth taking only after the build already functions without it.

rewardDecisionRules.condition: The aspect's primary Attack, Special, Cast, Sprint, or Omega slot is still empty.
rewardDecisionRules.reason: A functional core move adds reliable damage now and unlocks later scaling choices.

rewardDecisionRules.condition: The combat sequence spends Magick repeatedly and no recovery source sustains one full room.
rewardDecisionRules.reason: The build stops working when Magick runs out, so recovery comes before optional damage.

rewardDecisionRules.condition: The core Boon is secured and one of the three recommended compatible Hammers is offered.
rewardDecisionRules.reason: A top Hammer changes the weapon itself and is harder to replace than another non-core Boon or one level.

rewardDecisionRules.condition: Current Life or Death Defiance cannot reliably cover the next guardian.
rewardDecisionRules.reason: Surviving the route preserves all existing build value and progression rewards.

rewardDecisionRules.condition: A named permanent unlock is the current progression target and the build already clears ordinary rooms safely.
rewardDecisionRules.reason: The permanent resource advances the A-to-Z route without sacrificing a required combat fix.

rewardDecisionRules.condition: The core Boon exists, the build survives, and no top Hammer or missing resource loop is offered.
rewardDecisionRules.reason: A level on the repeatedly used core effect is more reliable than filling an unused move slot.

rewardDecisionRules.condition: Every prerequisite set is satisfied and the offered Duo or Legendary directly supports the completed package.
rewardDecisionRules.reason: The rare target is worth taking only after the build already functions without it.

rewardPriorities.reason: Fill the aspect's special damage slot before spending rewards on optional scaling.

rewardDecisionRules.condition: The aspect's primary Attack, Special, Cast, Sprint, or Omega slot is still empty.
rewardDecisionRules.reason: A functional core move adds reliable damage now and unlocks later scaling choices.

rewardDecisionRules.condition: The combat sequence spends Magick repeatedly and no recovery source sustains one full room.
rewardDecisionRules.reason: The build stops working when Magick runs out, so recovery comes before optional damage.

rewardDecisionRules.condition: The core Boon is secured and one of the three recommended compatible Hammers is offered.
rewardDecisionRules.reason: A top Hammer changes the weapon itself and is harder to replace than another non-core Boon or one level.

rewardDecisionRules.condition: Current Life or Death Defiance cannot reliably cover the next guardian.
rewardDecisionRules.reason: Surviving the route preserves all existing build value and progression rewards.

rewardDecisionRules.condition: A named permanent unlock is the current progression target and the build already clears ordinary rooms safely.
rewardDecisionRules.reason: The permanent resource advances the A-to-Z route without sacrificing a required combat fix.

rewardDecisionRules.condition: The core Boon exists, the build survives, and no top Hammer or missing resource loop is offered.
rewardDecisionRules.reason: A level on the repeatedly used core effect is more reliable than filling an unused move slot.

rewardDecisionRules.condition: Every prerequisite set is satisfied and the offered Duo or Legendary directly supports the completed package.
rewardDecisionRules.reason: The rare target is worth taking only after the build already functions without it.

rewardDecisionRules.condition: The aspect's primary Attack, Special, Cast, Sprint, or Omega slot is still empty.
rewardDecisionRules.reason: A functional core move adds reliable damage now and unlocks later scaling choices.

rewardDecisionRules.condition: The core Boon is secured and one of the three recommended compatible Hammers is offered.
rewardDecisionRules.reason: A top Hammer changes the weapon itself and is harder to replace than another non-core Boon or one level.

rewardDecisionRules.condition: Current Life or Death Defiance cannot reliably cover the next guardian.
rewardDecisionRules.reason: Surviving the route preserves all existing build value and progression rewards.

rewardDecisionRules.condition: A named permanent unlock is the current progression target and the build already clears ordinary rooms safely.
rewardDecisionRules.reason: The permanent resource advances the A-to-Z route without sacrificing a required combat fix.

rewardDecisionRules.condition: The core Boon exists, the build survives, and no top Hammer or missing resource loop is offered.
rewardDecisionRules.reason: A level on the repeatedly used core effect is more reliable than filling an unused move slot.

rewardDecisionRules.condition: Every prerequisite set is satisfied and the offered Duo or Legendary directly supports the completed package.
rewardDecisionRules.reason: The rare target is worth taking only after the build already functions without it.

rewardPriorities.reason: Fill the aspect's attack damage slot before spending rewards on optional scaling.
Take a compatible top-ranked Hammer after the first core Boon. No Hammer is required to make the build function.
Move maximum Life ahead of damage rewards when the current route cannot survive the next guardian reliably.
Use Poms after the core Boon exists so levels land on an effect the build repeatedly uses.
Take recovery only after the normal-move plan and immediate survival needs are covered.
Pursue a Duo or Legendary only after the build already contains a valid choice from every prerequisite set.

value.fallback: If neither a fatal-hit recovery nor Fishing Point access serves the current objective, use Frinos for unconditional maximum Life.
value.limitation: Its general combat value is less consistent than Life, Magick, critical chance, or mobility.
value.reason: The Heart Bond can protect a run while the Sense Bond supports a specific gathering target.
value.recommendation: Use Toula when an extra recovery effect or Fishing Point access advances the current objective.

value.fallback: If Magick limits an Omega build, use Hecuba. If survival is already stable and clear speed matters more, use Raki.
value.limitation: Frinos adds less clear speed than Familiars with offensive passive bonuses.
value.reason: The Life bonus improves every encounter and asks for no build-specific setup.
value.recommendation: Use Frinos while learning routes or whenever maximum Life is the main constraint.

value.fallback: If survival is uncertain, use Frinos. If the build already sustains its Magick and wants more damage, use Raki.
value.limitation: A build that rarely spends Magick gains less than it would from Life, critical chance, or mobility.
value.reason: The Magick bonus supports repeated Omega actions while the stun creates safer openings.
value.recommendation: Use Hecuba when an Omega-heavy build needs more maximum Magick and room control.

value.fallback: If predictable maximum Life matters more than dodge chance, use Frinos. If damage matters more than mobility, use Raki.
value.limitation: Dodge is less predictable than a larger Life pool and adds no direct build resource.
value.reason: The passive defensive mobility remains active without requiring a particular attack pattern.
value.recommendation: Use Gale when movement speed and dodge chance solve the current route or Fear condition.

value.fallback: If survival is uncertain, use Frinos. If Magick limits an Omega build, use Hecuba.
value.limitation: The random damage increase does not repair low Life, poor Magick recovery, or unsafe positioning.
value.reason: Critical chance can improve every damage source without changing the combat sequence.
value.recommendation: Use Raki when the build already survives reliably and benefits from universal critical chance.

value.fallback: If the encounter does not allow a long stationary channel, choose Wolf Howl for an aimed burst or Sky Fall for automatic pressure.
value.limitation: Channeling restricts movement and competes with the weapon's normal damage sequence.
value.reason: The beam can concentrate damage on a stationary or controlled target.
value.recommendation: Choose Lunar Ray when the build can create a safe channeling window.

value.fallback: If close-range landing is unsafe, choose Total Eclipse for a ranged delayed blast or Phase Shift for control.
value.limitation: Its close target area can be unsafe when the landing window is poorly timed.
value.reason: The effect resolves quickly and works without a slain enemy, long channel, or delayed target.
value.recommendation: Choose Wolf Howl for immediate area damage and repositioning.

value.fallback: If targets leave the marked area before the blast, choose Wolf Howl for immediate damage.
value.limitation: Mobile targets can leave before the fuse ends.
value.reason: The large area rewards bosses and groups that remain inside the marked zone.
value.recommendation: Choose Total Eclipse when a large delayed blast can be placed on a predictable target.

value.fallback: If damage must land immediately on one chosen area, choose Wolf Howl instead.
value.limitation: Random target selection can spread damage in crowded rooms.
value.reason: Repeated strikes add damage while Melinoe continues moving and using the weapon.
value.recommendation: Choose Sky Fall when automatic pressure fits a mobile build.

value.fallback: If the route's main obstacle is immune to transformation, choose Phase Shift for control that also works during bosses.
value.limitation: Bosses and other resistant targets remove much of its value.
value.reason: The seeking projectile can disable several susceptible foes and reduce incoming pressure.
value.recommendation: Choose Twilight Curse for control in dense normal encounters.

value.fallback: If the run already finishes with Life to spare, choose Phase Shift for prevention or a direct-damage Hex for faster clears.
value.limitation: It does not speed up rooms when the build already finishes with a large Life buffer.
value.reason: Direct healing repairs mistakes and its uses replenish at fountains.
value.recommendation: Choose Moon Water when health loss is the main reason runs end.

value.fallback: If rooms do not provide a useful enemy to raise, choose Sky Fall for automatic pressure without a kill requirement.
value.limitation: The Hex needs an eligible slain enemy and is unreliable at the start of a room or in some boss fights.
value.reason: A raised enemy adds damage and draws attention without replacing Melinoe's actions.
value.recommendation: Choose Night Bloom when encounters reliably provide a strong susceptible enemy to raise.

value.fallback: If lost Life, rather than unsafe attack windows, ends the run, choose Moon Water for direct healing.
value.limitation: It adds less immediate burst than a direct-damage Hex.
value.reason: Slowing the encounter creates room to attack, reposition, or recover without replacing the build's normal actions.
value.recommendation: Choose Phase Shift for a broadly safe Hex that preserves the current weapon sequence.

value.fallback: If interrupting the weapon sequence costs more than the transformation gains, choose Phase Shift instead.
value.limitation: Its separate abilities interrupt aspect-specific boon and weapon sequences.
value.reason: The transformation creates a protected damage window during dangerous encounters.
value.recommendation: Choose Dark Side when invulnerability is more valuable than continuing the normal weapon loop.

public.summary: Complete Unraveling a Fateful Bond. Starting on the following night, Hera is guaranteed in the first chamber until you accept her first boon.

rules: Accept a Zeus boon and enter Oceanus on two nights. Hermes then appears in person at the start of a later Underworld night and grants his first boon. Later Hermes rewards require that first meeting, cannot repeat in the same biome reward history, and are limited to two offers per night.

public.name: Hermes
public.summary: Accept a Zeus boon and enter Oceanus on two nights. Hermes then appears in person at the start of a later Underworld night and grants his first boon. Later Hermes rewards require that first meeting, cannot repeat in the same biome reward history, and are limited to two offers per night.

rules: After accepting both Demeter's and Poseidon's first boons, Hestia is guaranteed at the start of a later Underworld night until you accept her first boon.

rules: After accepting Apollo's first boon, Poseidon is guaranteed at the start of a later Underworld night until you accept his first boon. Demeter is offered first while neither first appearance is complete.

public.name: Poseidon
public.summary: After accepting Apollo's first boon, Poseidon is guaranteed at the start of a later Underworld night until you accept his first boon. Demeter is offered first while neither first appearance is complete.

rules: Accept a Hermes boon, then begin a later night. Chaos Gates have a 20% base chance in eligible rooms, do not appear while the Surface curse is active, and cannot recur within 10 rooms.

rules: Before his first boon, Zeus is forced through the rainy Erebus state after at least 3 completed nights, provided the previous 4 nights had no biome-state change. The next eligible Erebus opening guarantees Zeus. After accepting his first boon, he joins the normal Olympian pool.

rules: Requires you to advance Arachne's relationship to the required conversation.

fields.value: Gain 30 Armor. While you have at least 1 Armor, gain +2 Armor after each location.

value.fallback: Use Luckier Tooth when chip damage makes preserving Armor unrealistic.
value.limitation: After all Armor is lost, it cannot rebuild itself and should be replaced at the next cabinet.
value.reason: The starting Armor absorbs mistakes, and every chamber cleared before it breaks adds more Armor.
value.recommendation: Take it through early regions while you can preserve its Armor between chambers.
value.switchWhenInactive: At the next keepsake cabinet, replace it after its Armor, healing, or Magick reserve is empty.

public.name: Silken Sash
public.summary: Gain 30 Armor. While you have at least 1 Armor, gain +2 Armor after each location.

rules: Requires you to advance Athena's relationship to the required conversation.

fields.value: While you have no Death Defiance, Athena may appear once this night with at least Common boons.

value.fallback: Use Luckier Tooth before the run if you still have a keepsake cabinet and need a guaranteed recovery.
value.limitation: It does nothing while any Death Defiance remains and can trigger only once per night.
value.reason: It can add one Athena encounter with defensive boons when the run has no Death Defiance left.
value.recommendation: Equip it only after every Death Defiance is gone and an Athena encounter can rescue the night.
value.switchWhenInactive: At the next keepsake cabinet, replace it after its remaining uses reach zero.

public.name: Gorgon Amulet
public.summary: While you have no Death Defiance, Athena may appear once this night with at least Common boons.

rules: Requires you to advance Moros's relationship to the required conversation.

fields.value: When first you fall to 0 Life in an encounter, become invulnerable. Clear it in time for 30 Life restored.

value.fallback: Use Luckier Tooth for an automatic recovery that does not depend on clearing the room in time.
value.limitation: If the room cannot be cleared before the invulnerability expires, it provides no recovery.
value.reason: The first fatal hit becomes a timed chance to clear the encounter and return with 30 Life.
value.recommendation: Level it early when one difficult room, not steady chip damage, is ending promising nights.
value.switchWhenInactive: Keep it while its condition supports the current route, then replace it when another keepsake solves a more immediate constraint.

public.name: Engraved Pin
public.summary: When first you fall to 0 Life in an encounter, become invulnerable. Clear it in time for 30 Life restored.

rules: Requires you to advance Charon's relationship to the required conversation.

value.fallback: Use the build's god keepsake when securing the first core boon matters more than an early purchase.
value.limitation: It adds no combat power unless the extra Gold is converted into a useful purchase.
value.reason: Its 100 Gold is granted immediately, so the keepsake can be replaced at the first cabinet without losing value.
value.recommendation: Start with it when an early shop or expensive Well purchase is part of the route plan.
value.switchWhenInactive: At the next keepsake cabinet, replace it after the starting Gold has been granted.

fields.value: After the next Guardian, activate two random inactive Arcana Cards at rank I, II, or III according to this Keepsake's rank.

value.fallback: Use Knuckle Bones when defeating that Guardian is less certain than benefiting from the reward afterward.
value.limitation: The cards are random, and the effect is wasted if the inactive pool offers little value.
value.reason: Defeating the next Guardian activates two inactive Arcana Cards at the keepsake's current rank.
value.recommendation: Equip it before a Guardian when two random inactive Arcana Cards could improve the rest of the night.
value.switchWhenInactive: At the next keepsake cabinet, replace it after its remaining uses reach zero.

rules: Requires you to advance Odysseus's relationship to the required conversation.

fields.value: The next Guardian starts with 5% less Life. You take 10% less damage from Guardians.

value.fallback: Use Luckier Tooth when ordinary rooms are consuming more Life than the Guardian.
value.limitation: It contributes little in ordinary rooms, so do not equip it early when reaching the Guardian is still unreliable.
value.reason: The next Guardian starts with 5% less Life, and all Guardian damage against you is reduced by 10%.
value.recommendation: Equip it before the region whose Guardian is the run's remaining obstacle.
value.switchWhenInactive: At the next keepsake cabinet, replace it after its limited guardian effect has been consumed and another guardian remains.

public.name: Knuckle Bones
public.summary: The next Guardian starts with 5% less Life. You take 10% less damage from Guardians.

rules: Requires you to advance Medea's relationship to the required conversation.

fields.value: After taking 250 total damage this night, your Omega moves deal 20%, 30%, or 40% more damage according to this Keepsake's rank.

value.fallback: Use the opening god keepsake when the Omega build still lacks its core boon or Magick recovery.
value.limitation: It offers nothing before activation and rewards a damage total that safer runs may never reach.
value.reason: After the damage threshold is met, its permanent Omega damage bonus can carry the remaining regions.
value.recommendation: Use it on an Omega-heavy build only when taking 250 damage during the night is plausible.
value.switchWhenInactive: Keep it while its condition supports the current route, then replace it when another keepsake solves a more immediate constraint.

value.fallback: Use Knuckle Bones for a broader Guardian bonus when the previous defeat is not the only problem.
value.limitation: It adds no damage against other foes and loses purpose after the targeted obstacle is overcome.
value.reason: Its 20% damage bonus applies directly to the last foe that defeated you.
value.recommendation: Equip it for a rematch when one known foe or Guardian ended the previous night.

Eris does not apply the curse when Melinoe has no Death Defiance and is at or below 50% Life.
